messages.subject: About multidimensional model
parts:
Hi dear mirt family,

I'm new in this group and in R. I need your suggestion.
I'm developing a scale about organizational behavior for my PhD disertation. I'm in the validation process now. The scale has 53 items and they are polytomous data. According to explaratory factor analysis on SPSS, it has 3 dimensions. So, do I have to use multidimensional model on the item response theory? (If yes, do I exclude the items accordig to a? ) Or is it possible to use unidimensional model? Mirt is so complicated for beginners :(
Thanks.

messages.subject: Re: About multidimensional model
parts:
On Fri, Jan 29, 2021 at 2:14 PM Esengul Elibol <esengu...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi dear mirt family,

I'm new in this group and in R. I need your suggestion.
I'm developing a scale about organizational behavior for my PhD disertation. I'm in the validation process now. The scale has 53 items and they are polytomous data. According to explaratory factor analysis on SPSS, it has 3 dimensions.

I'm not sure what this means. Was this a linear factor analysis using correlation statistics? If so, the structure may not be 3 dimensional at all due to artifacts based on correlations. Basically, more information is required before we can answer your question.

So, do I have to use multidimensional model on the item response theory? (If yes, do I exclude the items accordig to a? ) Or is it possible to use unidimensional model? Mirt is so complicated for beginners :(

It depends on your theory, the type of data you have available, the models with which you want to fit (and their respective dimensions), and so on. It's a very broad question you're asking, and my general recommendation would be to become more acquainted with IRT methods, and how they relate to things like factor analysis before moving forward with complicated models like multidimensional IRT. HTH.

Phil

 
Thanks.
